subject: Observability export and SIEM integration for Globex Private Deployment

Subject: Observability export and SIEM integration for Globex Private Deployment

Hi Alice and Globex team,

Thanks for taking time to review this with us. Per our kick-off call, attached is an initial design doc (redwood-private-obsv-design-v1.pdf) that outlines three integration options for shipping logs/metrics/traces from the Globex private deployment (VPC / on-prem enclave) into your SIEM:

- Direct HEC (HTTPS) push with mutual TLS + IP allowlist (preferred for low-latency logs)
- Local forwarder (syslog TLS) inside the customer network that tunnels to a Redwood-managed collector via an outbound egress proxy
- Buffered batch export (S3-compatible staging) for air-gapped/local-only scenarios

A few things we want to validate in this review:
1) Allowed egress endpoints and firewall rules — can Globex allow outbound to a small set of IPs or a DNS name?
2) Certificate lifecycle — do you prefer client cert rotation managed by Globex or a short-lived token we can pull from an internal vault?
3) Field mapping & retention — what SIEM indexes and retention windows do you need?
4) Request tracing — how do you want request IDs surfaced across the stack (header name, sampling rate)?

If helpful, we can provide a PoC HEC endpoint and a sample curl+mTLS script to validate connectivity. Next step proposal: design review with your security and infra owners on Tue Nov 2.

Regards,

Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 1, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for taking time to review this with us. Per our kick-off call, attached is an initial design doc...

Thanks Jonas — the options look reasonable. A few clarifications from our side before the review:

- Firewall / egress: we prefer DNS allowlisting rather than IPs where possible; however vendor-managed endpoints must be documented for SOC.
- Retention: audit logs must be retained for 7 years in our Splunk instance; operational logs 90 days.
- SIEM: primary target is Splunk HEC (https://splunk.globex.internal:8088/services/collector). We will provide a HEC token in the secure workspace (we won't paste tokens over email).
- Mapping: we need a recommended Splunk index and sourcetype mapping (audit -> index:globex_audit, op -> index:globex_ops).
- Tracing hooks: prefer OpenTelemetry headers and x-request-id for cross-service correlation. Sampling: 1% global with 100% on error traces.

Attached is our requirements spreadsheet (globex-siem-requirements.xlsx) with current indexes and retention. For the Nov 2 review we will have security (me + Carlos) and an infra engineer on the call.

Also: long-term key management — we will need rotation certificates on a quarterly cadence and an audit trail of cert issuance.

Regards,

Alice Dubois
Senior Security Engineer | Globex Corp
alice.dubois@globex.com

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@globex.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability export and SIEM integration for Globex Private Deployment

Hi Alice — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. We've sketched a recommended integration that meets your audit and retention constraints while keeping latency and cost in check. Summary below plus concrete examples (we'll attach a small script with HEC mTLS example).

Recommended approach (middle ground):
- Primary path: local forwarder (vector/rsyslog) inside the VPC that forwards out to a dedicated Redwood HEC endpoint over mTLS. This keeps control inside Globex network and minimizes open ports.
- Fallback: if outbound is blocked, forwarder should buffer to a local disk and batch-upload to a Globex-managed S3-compatible bucket that Redwood can pull from inside a controlled window (airgap mode).

Network / auth details:
- Egress: allow DNS name hec-redwood-prod.globex.redwood.ai and ports 443/8088; we will publish the specific IP ranges in the security binder before cutover.
- mTLS: client certs issued by Globex CA; we will support both cert-based auth and short-lived JWT bearer tokens (rotated via Vault). Cert rotation: schedule quarterly; we recommend acme-style automation if Globex can run a cert agent.
- Mutual validation: Redwood will present a server cert pinned to our CA; Globex validates client cert CN against allowed list.

Splunk mapping / retention:
- Suggested mapping:
  - index=globex_audit, sourcetype=redwood:audit for audit events (7y retention)
  - index=globex_ops, sourcetype=redwood:syslog for operational logs (90d retention)
  - index=globex_traces, sourcetype=redwood:otel for trace exports (30d)

Tracing hooks / instrumentation:
- Header contract: accept and propagate x-request-id and traceparent (W3C Trace Context). If x-request-id not present, Redwood runtime will synthesize one and return it in responses.
- Sampling: default 1% global plus 100% capture for any >=500 HTTP / error spans; we can configure per-route samplers.
- OpenTelemetry: we emit OTLP-compatible spans; Redwood can deliver these either via in-band exporter to your OTLP endpoint or as batched HEC events with structured JSON for Splunk.

Operational considerations:
- Backpressure: forwarder should use persistent disk queueing and apply log-throttling for noisy sources. Redwood runtime honors Retry-After from SIEM and supports exponential backoff for HEC responses >=429.
- Bandwidth: we estimate steady-state egress ~20 MB/min for initial pilot (30 nodes, normal traffic). We will run a 48-hour traffic sampling to refine numbers.
- Audit evidence: Redwood will produce export logs (who exported what, timestamps) for SOC-2 evidence; these can be pushed to index=globex_audit.

Next items we will deliver before the review:
- hec-mtls-example.sh (cURL + client cert)
- Sample field mapping JSON (flattened event -> Splunk KV pairs)
- A short runbook for cert rotation and emergency rekey

If that looks good, Jonas will coordinate a test window and we can exchange test certs via your secure workspace.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park

kimberly_park@redwood.ai

- Redwood to stand up a non-prod HEC endpoint and provide IP/DNS and example scripts — owner: Jonas — target: 2026-11-09
- 48-hour traffic capture & sizing run inside Globex (sample agents) — owner: Globex infra — target: 2026-11-16
- Field mapping review and retention config (joint) — owners: Kimberly + Globex SIEM — target: 2026-11-18
- SOC evidence checklist exchange (who does what) — owners: Marissa + Globex security — target: 2026-11-12

Risks / mitigations:
- If outbound DNS/IP restriction blocks us, we will use the buffered S3 approach for cutover windows.
- For strict airgap customers we will provide an offline evidence bundle workflow and a signed transfer protocol.

Please reply with any schedule conflicts or additional owners you want added. I'll open an INT-452 ticket and attach the artifacts (see link).
